Reference data naming the analytics ORE's run document can ask for: NPV,
cashflows, curves, simulation, XVA, initial margin, sensitivity, stress, SIMM
and the rest. The element's type attribute is a free string in ORE's schema;
this is the vocabulary the shipped run documents actually use, and it is what
makes the attribute a foreign key rather than free text.
Thirty-five types are in use across the corpus, and their parameter sets barely
overlap: xva takes around seventy parameters, simulation sixty, sensitivity
thirty, and several types one flag. That is why each type owns a table for its
parameters and this table names it, in parameter_entity, rather than every

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Reference data table defining valid concurrency policies for report definitions.
Concurrency policies control what happens when a scheduler trigger fires
for a report definition that already has a running instance.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.

One Parameter element inside one Analytic of the run document that a configuration describes: the value, and the definition that says what it means. A row is keyed to a definition in ore_parameter whose scope is the analytic and whose subtype is the analytic type code, so adding a parameter is a lookup row and never a column.

One row per Analytic element in the run document that a configuration describes: which analytic to run, in what order, and whether it is on. A report definition binds a shared configuration, and the configuration owns its analytics, so reports that run the same analytics share one set of rows. The parameters of an analytic are rows of configuration_analytic_parameter.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.

One Parameter of the Markets block in a run document: a market role, and the market configuration the run binds to it. The block belongs to the configuration that describes the run, so reports that share a configuration share its market roles. The role is a free string in ORE's schema, and the value names a configuration set built in todaysmarket.xml, which ores.analytics owns. This table holds the binding, not the configuration it names.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One value. The value is text because the definition says what it is: the
value domain on ore_parameter decides whether this is a currency, a
date, a boolean, a tenor or a reference, and the mapper writes it into the
document accordingly. Storing it as text is not the same as storing an
untyped blob, because the meaning comes from a foreign key rather than from
position keeps the order the document wrote the parameters in.

Reference data naming the kinds of configuration a report can bind: the ORE
run itself, a stress library, a sensitivity analysis, a simulation, a SIMM
calibration, a credit simulation, a historical return set, a Basel traffic
light set, and the curve and reference documents.
This is a seeded vocabulary, not free text. A discriminator stored as a bare
code cannot be constrained, counted or joined, which is why every
configuration carries one of these rows by foreign key. Adding a kind is a
row here plus a workflow, never a column on the report definition.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The name is ours; the detail lives with the component named by
owning_component. A report binds a configuration through
report_configuration, so several reports share one configuration without
copying it, and the kind of configuration it is comes from
configuration_type by foreign key rather than from a text code.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The detail row of one reporting.eod_cut_authorisation or
reporting.ipv_cut_authorisation approval request: the cut the request
authorises, and the counts of the body the decider is asked to sign.
A request is a header. What it is about lives here, keyed by the request's own
id, exactly as a proposed published set lives in
ores.marketdata.curve_publish and is keyed by its request. The subject is one
fact and no more: the cut whose body was frozen. The counts travel beside it
because the decider reads them before answering and the cut's own record states
them only by reading the body's parts one at a time: the deals the population
held at the instant, the published sets in use at it, and the gaps that would
have stopped the take, which is zero for any body a request was raised for.
applied_at and applied_by are the record of the apply. Both are empty while
the request waits, and both are written in one act when the approved request is
applied to the cut: the instant the authorisation was stamped and the account
that stamped it. The row is bitemporal, so the applied version is a new version
of the same row and the history holds the unapplied subject beside it.
request_id is the natural key, so a request authorises one cut and no second
apply can find a row to write.
The row is not a client's to write: the take writes it with the body, and the
apply stamps it. A client reads it to decide a request or to audit a cut.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Reference data table of the families a cut kind belongs to. A family groups
the kinds whose body is the same and whose instant comes from the same place.
The family fixes the body rule and the source of the instant; a kind inside it
fixes the rest. The end of day family holds the ordinary close, the month end
and the year end, because all three fix the same four inputs at the same
centre's close and differ only in what the occasion covers and how long the cut
is kept. A family of one is not a wasted row: it states the body rule and the
instant source for every kind that will join it.
The families are end_of_day, start_of_day, verification, intraday and
consumer. The consumer family is the one whose instant the run supplies, which
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One part of a cut's body that the assembly could not fill: the part, the item
inside it and the reason it could not be filled.
A cut that fixed the data and omitted a part it could not read would look
smaller than it is. The gap list is the answer to that: the body that could not
be assembled is a fact a person acts on, and the cut's own page is where the
list is read. A take that could not close a gap saves the attempt as an
incomplete cut and raises no approval request, because a decider would be asked
to sign a body that does not meet the definition.
The parts are the four inputs the body holds: the market data, the deal
population, the reference data, and the engine and the code.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Reference data table of the kinds of cut. A kind is not a sentence in a
knowledge page: it is a row a person maintains, because four of the facts it
carries are decisions a firm changes and reads back.
approval_kind_code is a nullable foreign key to the inbox's own lookup. It is
the whole of the authorisation rule: the end of day family's kinds point at
reporting.eod_cut_authorisation, whose decider is Finance, the verification
kind points at reporting.ipv_cut_authorisation, whose decider is Market Risk,
and the start of day, intraday and consumer kinds point at nothing. A screen
draws the words from the key's target and a dash where the key is null, so a
firm that gives the close to another function changes one approval kind and no
Nothing a screen prints about authorisation is stored: the signed-or-not a
person reads is derived from this column.
retention_months states the periods the design fixes: 25 for the ordinary
close and the open, 84 for the month end and the verification, 120 for the year
end, 3 for the intraday view and 1 for the live view. retention_destination_code
names where a cut goes when it leaves the warm tier. No storage tier lookup
exists yet, so the column carries a check on the codes this round knows and the
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Reference data table of the rules a cut kind may name. A report holds a cut
selection, and the selection is a rule: the run executes it against the date the
report covers, the report's scope and the scope's rates centre, and the answer is
one concrete cut or a refusal.
A rule is read from the kind at the moment of the resolution and never copied
onto a cut or a report, because a report resolving today must follow today's
rule and not the rule in force when the report was defined.
*The resolution*. A kind whose occasion no rule can resolve names the_cut_named,
and the report reaches its cuts by pinning one rather than by selecting a kind.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The record of one cut: a body of data fixed at one timepoint, the four inputs
the valuation reads, the gaps the assembly could not fill, and the acts that
made it. A report's run resolves its selection to a cut and prices from the
body the cut names, so a result is reproduced by naming its cut rather than by
The state a reader sees is a function of these facts and is stored nowhere, as
the published set's state is. Draft when no taking instant holds and no gap
stands; incomplete when no taking instant holds and a gap stands; taken when the
body is fixed, the kind requires an authorisation and none is recorded; in use
when the body is fixed and the kind requires none; authorised when an approval
is recorded; refused when a refusal is recorded; superseded when a later cut of
the same kind and scope holds its place.
The label a person quotes is derived from the kind, the scope and the timepoint,
and the take ordinal where a body is taken more than once for one occasion:
EOD.ACME-LONDON.2026-10-06 and EOD.ACME-LONDON.2026-10-06.2. A live cut
carries its instant to the second instead of an ordinal. No column holds the
The retention is a copy and not a read: a cut takes the kind's retention_months,
retention_destination_code and legal_hold_default when it is taken, so a
later change to the kind does not move the retention of a body already fixed.
The indicative mark is a second copy for the same reason: a cut records whether a
result priced from it is indicative, taken from its kind at the take, because the
mark is a fact about the body and not about its state.
Nothing removes a cut today; the archive is a later task.

The market and trade building part of a named engine settings configuration. How the engine builds the market and the trades, and what it does when that fails. A change here changes the numbers. A column that is null means the engine default,
and a configuration with no row in this part uses the default for every setting in it. A write to this part bumps the version of the
central engine_settings row in the same transaction.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
A number-changing group of engine run settings never changes in place. A write
to such a group is a proposal: the values the person asked for are held here,
one row for each setting of the group, and the version in force keeps the rows a
run reads until the request is signed off.
The apply reads the rows of an approved request and writes the group it names
with the values stated here, so a proposal that waits changes no part.
A row names the setting by its code, which is the group and the column joined,
so a proposal survives a change to the columns of a part.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The execution part of a named engine settings configuration. How the engine runs and logs. A change here does not change the numbers. A column that is null means the engine default,
and a configuration with no row in this part uses the default for every setting in it. A write to this part bumps the version of the
central engine_settings row in the same transaction.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.

The fixings and cash flows part of a named engine settings configuration. Which fixings and cash flows count in a run. A change here changes the numbers. A column that is null means the engine default,
and a configuration with no row in this part uses the default for every setting in it. A write to this part bumps the version of the
central engine_settings row in the same transaction.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One setting of one group, as the screen lists it: the column its value travels
under, and the ORE parameter that documents it and that names its value set. The
group's settings are what a screen shows and what a write to the group accepts,
so a setting is data here and no longer a list in the browser's server code.
The control the screen draws and the values the setting accepts are not stated
here. They belong to the value set of the ORE parameter, which the Setup scope
link names, so one rule serves this table, the pricing screen and the write path.
Whether a setting changes the numbers a run computes is stated here, so the
screen can warn a person before a write that moves them.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The engine settings a screen draws come in groups, and a configuration keeps one
row of each group it sets. The group states the code the screen and the service
travel the part under, the words a person reads and the place it takes in the
screen. The settings of the group are rows of engine_settings_group_setting.
Until this table held the groups, a list of them lived in the browser's server
code, so a new group of settings took a change of code. The list is data now, so
the screen draws the groups the data holds, in the order the data states.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The central row of a named engine settings configuration. A report definition binds the configuration through
report_configuration, in the slot of configuration type engine_settings, as it binds its pricing engines. The row holds
only the identity. The settings live in three parts, each its own table keyed by this row: engine_settings_fixings,
engine_settings_building and engine_settings_execution. A part that has no row means the engine default for every
setting in it. A write to any part bumps the version of this row in the same transaction.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Reference data naming the files an ORE run reads and writes. A file type is one
parameter of the run document that carries a file name: a Setup parameter such as
conventionsFile, or the parameter of an analytic such as the outputFileName of npv.
The table gives each its well known name, so a configuration never repeats a file
name and the export looks the name up when it writes a file.
The names come from the shipped ORE samples. Each is the most common name the samples
give the file, and sample_count out of sample_total records how many use it.
Names that embed a date are set aside, because a date is a value of the run.
A name may be a pattern with a key, for example portfolio_{{BOOK_ID}}.xml, for a file
that a run splits. The table can hold the pattern. Splitting is a later task.
The table lists names and patterns. It does not hold the content of a file.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
A value set governs a leaf, and a leaf is carried by a column of a table the
projection writes. The map names the leaf; this table names the columns that
carry it, so a guard can start from the row it is about to write and reach the
rule without knowing either the document's path or the parameter contract.
The row exists because the same leaf is carried by many columns: DayCounter is
a column of every curve family table. One map row, many columns, one rule.
The xpath stays here because it is the leaf's address in the document, which is
what the import and the convention screens show. The entity, the table and the
column are what the guard needs, because a trigger sees a row of one table.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Ore Parameter Setting Value Set Table
The junction between a setting and the set of values it allows. It is keyed by
the setting, (scope, name), and not by a parameter row, because the contract
holds one row per product type and the allowed values are the same for all of
them. A setting has one set today, so the pair is unique; the junction is a
table so a setting may draw from more than one set later without a migration.
The code is the scope and the name joined with a colon, for example
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Every configuration parameter holds one value, and this says what that value
is: a currency, a date, a boolean, an integer, a tenor, a document reference,
or a list. Where the value names something in the model, referenced_entity
names the entity it points at, so the mapper knows what to write into the
document and a reader knows what the value means.
A malformed org header makes this loader fail in a misleading way: a line
that does not start at column zero, or a stray character before a #+ keyword,
leaves the entity type unresolved and the generator writes files called
unknown_* rather than reporting the bad line. Check the header first when a
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Ore Parameter Value Set Catalogue Table
A parameter whose values are other ORE Studio data names a catalogue here: the
tenors, the currencies, the currency pairs, the sensitivity templates, the
instrument codes, the calendars, the day counters, the conventions. The values
are the catalogue's current rows, read through a view that presents the value
and the label, so nothing is copied into the parameter tables and a row retired
from the catalogue is refused by the same read.
Only a registered relation can be read, and its shape is checked when the
registry loads. A catalogue is data, so adding one is a row here and the view it
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Ore Parameter Value Set Value Table
One value of an enumerated set, with the label a person reads, where it sits in
the combo and whether it may still be chosen. The contract is the one place a
value list lives: the per-pair settings table no longer carries one.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
A parameter states its storage type in the value domain and its allowed values
here. A set is enumerated, in which case its values are rows of
ore_parameter_value_set_value, or it is a catalogue, in which case the values
are the current rows of another ORE Studio catalogue named by
ore_parameter_value_set_catalogue. A range and a regular expression carry
their rules on the set itself. A boolean is the built-in pair true and false.
The kind states what one value may be. The cardinality states how many values
the document writes: one, or a comma separated list of them. They are separate
facts because a period and a list of periods obey the same rule and differ only
in how many the element holds, and ORE writes both into a single string. Keeping
them apart is what lets a screen draw one control instead of one control per
combination, and what lets the guard check every item of a list rather than wave
The set is shared by every parameter that names it, so one list of values serves
every product type and every pair that takes the setting.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
An ORE document spells some of its values in a vocabulary it defines: a
Currency, a DayCounter, a BusinessDayConvention. A leaf with one of those
names takes that vocabulary's value set wherever it appears, so the declaration
is stated once here rather than inferred from the name inside a generator.
A row says which element name, in which schema, takes which value set, and where
the rule comes from: the ORE source that reads the element, or the curator who
decided it. These rows are seeded from ore_parameter_vocabularies.json, and
the generator that links a curve's leaves to their sets reads that same
declaration, so a vocabulary added to it is a row here and needs no change to
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The vocabulary of ORE XML. A row documents one leaf of one ORE document: an
attribute or an element that holds a value. schema_name names the XML schema
of the document, for example ore.xsd, and xpath is the path to the leaf in
a document of that schema. The two together say which leaf this is.
ORE writes the parameters of ore.xml as a name and a value inside a block.
For them scope names the block (Setup, Markets, an analytic), subtype
narrows it, and name is the parameter, so the three give the same path as
xpath. position keeps the order the document wrote, because a document that
is not reproducible in order is not reproducible.
165 of the 218 parameter names observed in the shipped corpus belong to
exactly one analytic kind, which is why the name alone is not the key.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
A cashflow is not a metric. A metric states one figure about a subject; a
cashflow states a row per payment, keyed by the leg and the payment number, and
the stressed families state each of its figures three times, as a base, a
scenario and the difference between them.
The row here is therefore narrow, and keeps the cashflow's own keys: one figure,
named by its heading, with the part of the stressed comparison it states. A
family of cashflows adds no column to this table, and no figure of a cashflow is
flattened into report_metric, because the keys that make a cashflow a cashflow
have no place in a metric.
The row is written once, with the run, and never edited; a correction is a new
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
This is how a report definition reaches its configuration: one row per
configuration it binds, where the configuration type is the slot and the
configuration fills it. Several reports may fill the same slot with the same
configuration, so a configuration is never copied to be shared, and adding a
slot is not a column on the report definition.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The persistent template for a report. Describes what to run, when to run it,
how to handle concurrent executions, and how much of the processing pipeline a
run executes. Type-specific configuration (e.g. risk parameters) lives in a
The run configuration is held here rather than in the environment so that a run
is reproducible from the database alone. pre_processing and post_processing
name, for each substitutable phase, whether the phase runs or is replaced by a
Lifecycle is managed through the report_definition_lifecycle FSM machine.
fsm_state_id points to the current state in ores_dq_fsm_states_tbl.
scheduler_job_id links to ores_scheduler_job_definitions_tbl.id and is set
by the scheduler service when the definition is activated (state: active).
It is cleared when the definition is suspended or archived.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One error a report run produced, held against the run. A report run is one
execution of a report definition, and a run whose analytics fail is still a run
that completed: the engine finished, wrote its report, and said in its own log
that a trade would not build. Those errors are facts about the run, they belong
to it, and they are what this table holds.
An error is a fact about an instant: it is written once and never changed. The
model therefore states :current_state: and :immutable: in the * SQL **
does. A current-state immutable table has no validity window and no audit tail:
there is no version, no valid_from/valid_to, and no modified_by,
performed_by, change_reason_code or change_commentary. Because it has no
audit tail, the time is a column of its own, event_time.
event_time is the moment the errors were collected from the run's output. The
canonical rows do state the engine's own time, as the text the engine wrote, and
the service's log row keeps it; this column does not hold it. The recorder writes
the collection instant because it is an instant the service can state about its
own act, and storing the engine's text as a timestamp here would put two
different facts in one column. A story that needs the engine's instant adds a
A row says four things: how bad the error is, what it is about, what it said,
and which subject it names. The first is severity. The second is scope_code,
drawn from the engine's own vocabulary, and it is what places the error:
Trade on the trade, Analytics on the analytic, Curve on the curve, and
Report on the run itself. The third is message, the engine's own words.
The fourth is subject and subject_id, a discriminator and a value, holding
the identifier of the thing the error names: trade and a trade id,
analytic and an analytic type, curve and a curve id. It is a discriminator
and a value rather than one column because the ids are of different kinds — a
trade id is a UUID the portfolio builder minted, a curve id is a free-text name
such as [IndexCurve(GBP-SONIA,Yield/GBP/GBP1D)] — and one column holding
both would be a text column no reader can key on. It is not a database foreign
key for the same reason: the engine names trades by its own ids and curves by
their ORE names, and neither is a key any table here holds. The pair is stored
so that a screen can find every error about one subject, and it is a
discriminator rather than a fixed column per kind because the engine adds
sub-fields to the groups it already has, as the corpus shows it doing when an
scope_code and subject are not the same question. The scope is the group the
engine emitted, which is what the error is about at the level the engine named
it; the subject is the particular thing, and it can be narrower than the scope.
An Analytics error that names a tradeId is about that trade and not about
the analytic as a whole, and its subject says so.
A run that fails before the engine sees it, because a workflow step did not
complete, produces a row too, with scope Report. That is why the table is one
table rather than two: a reader opening a report wants its errors in one place.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The vocabulary a report error's scope is drawn from. The engine that computes a
report states the scope of every error it emits, in its structured log, as a
group. The codes here are those group names verbatim, so the model adds no
classification of its own: the engine says Trade and the row says Trade.
Report is the only code this model states rather than copies. Every other code
is a string the engine writes, and a code the engine writes that is not a row
here is a vocabulary the engine has grown: the row is refused, loudly, rather
than stored with a scope no reader can place.
An immutable artifact created by the assemble_bundle workflow step.
Records the object-storage keys where the MsgPack-serialised trades
and market data blobs produced during gather_trades and
gather_market_data are stored, and the version of each trade the run
read, as a JSON object keyed by trade id.
One bundle is created per report instance execution. The bundle is
consumed downstream by prepare_ore_package to repackage the data as
a tarball for the compute grid.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Reference data naming the kinds of report instance. A report instance is one
execution of a report definition, and its kind says what that execution does:
- production prepares the engine's input, computes it on the grid and records the
results. It is the kind of every instance the scheduler creates.
- package prepares the engine's input and stops. It produces the packages that the
compute grid would receive for the report and computes nothing, so a developer can
inspect a report's packages and run them in ORE on their own machine.
The kind is a property of the run and not of the definition: one definition has
instances of both kinds. A package instance is a real instance, with its own run
token scope, storage keys and lifecycle, so the steps that prepare the input work for
it unchanged. The concurrency policy of a definition counts production instances only.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
A single execution of a report_definition. Created automatically when the
scheduler fires a trigger for an active definition.
Lifecycle is managed through the report_instance_lifecycle FSM machine.
fsm_state_id points to the current state in ores_dq_fsm_states_tbl.
started_at is NULL when the instance is cancelled or skipped before execution
begins. completed_at is NULL while running or in a terminal-before-start state.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One figure a run produced, at one subject and one observation date, with the
qualifiers that say what the figure is about. Every family whose row is keys,
qualifiers and figures lands here, and family says which family it came from.
The row is written once, with the run, and never edited; a correction is a new
run. A figure the engine stated as its null string is not here at all, because
there is nothing to store. The subject_id is the engine's own identifier, such
as a trade id or a netting set id, so it is text and not a uuid.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One value a run stated as text rather than as a figure. Some outputs say what a
run was about rather than what it computed: the pricing engine and model a trade
used, the market objects and risk factors a portfolio depends on, the indices and
counterparties it names, and the calibrated model. Each value is a name and its
text, about a trade when the file names one, with the number beside it when the
engine stated the value as a double.
The row is written once, with the run, and never edited; a correction is a new
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One row per report trigger. A trigger is how a run is admitted, and it is of two
types: a person asks for the run now, or a schedule asks for it later. The
scheduler does not write this table. Its job publishes a trigger event, and the
reporting service records the trigger here and admits the run, so both types
reach the same handler and differ only in the payload.
The rows are append-only, so the model states :current_state:: an event is a
fact about an instant, and the bi-temporal pair has no meaning on it. A
current-state immutable table has no audit tail, so the actor and the time are
columns of its own and there is no version and no validity window. The table is
plain, not a hypertable: ores.iam.auth_event is one because logins are high
volume, and triggers are a handful a day.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Reference data naming the types of report trigger. A report run is admitted by
a trigger, and a trigger is one of two types:
- on_demand is a run a person asks for now, by naming the report within the
party they are signed in to.
- scheduled is a run a schedule asks for later. The scheduler job publishes a
trigger event when it fires, and a scheduled trigger names the job.
The type is deliberately named _type and not _kind, so it is not confused
with report_instance.kind, which says what a run does, production or package,

Many-to-many junction between report types and configuration types: one row
for each configuration type a run of the report type cannot start without. A
risk report needs pricing engines, today's market, curve configuration and
conventions whatever its analytics; a configuration type is needed by more than
one report type. Starting a report checks that its definition binds one
configuration of every type its report type requires.

Reference data table defining valid report type classifications.
Report types are managed by the system tenant. A report type names the
workflow its reports run and, through the report type configuration type
junction, the configuration types a run requires.
Associates a risk report configuration with the books it should include.
An empty set (no rows for a given risk_report_config_id) means all books
within the selected portfolios are included.
This is a temporal junction table: entries are closed when removed, preserving
historical scope records alongside the config version history.
Associates a risk report configuration with the portfolios it should include.
An empty set (no rows for a given risk_report_config_id) means all portfolios
visible to the tenant are included.
This is a temporal junction table: entries are closed when removed, preserving
historical scope records alongside the config version history.

The ORE-level run settings that risk report definitions of a party share: the base currency, the market data of the run and the folders and log file of the package. The engine settings are not here. They are a named configuration of their own, engine_settings, that the definition binds in its own slot. A report definition binds this configuration through report_configurations, in the slot of configuration type risk_report_config, as it binds its pricing engines. The analytics it runs, and their parameters, are rows of configuration_analytic and configuration_analytic_parameter. Portfolio and book scope live in separate temporal junction tables keyed by this row.
